### Subtypes in copied records

Ordinary-source and reviewed packages also accept the tested `Nat` Subtype
fields in acyclic copied records and variants. Use the generated record and
active-case fields with the usual GMP integer values; do not add proof fields.
Each input site keeps its selected Lean constructor. Two uses of the same record
can select different constructors and normalize the same payload differently.

Copied results expose values Lean has already constructed. They need no input
constructor selection, including in standalone result-only packages. The
[installed C/C++ checks](../evidence/nominal-subtype-native-acceptance-20261011.md)
cover repeated and nested records, active variants, transparent aliases,
structural containers, mixed `Fin` guards, 100-bit results and recovery after
rejection. C retains existing output and borrowed input on rejection. Keep the
generated initialization and cleanup calls described above.

Both source routes reproduce packages from two author roots, install without
the author sources and replay unchanged callers after relocating the installed
tree. These runs used Linux x64/glibc 2.36, GCC 12.2 and Lean 4.32.2. They do not
measure constructor/source entries or memory, or establish hosted release-floor
acceptance. Other primitive-base nominal fixtures, refined callbacks, owned,
recursive, dependent and broader generic Subtypes remain pending.
